title: Mardi Gras and Sunday wagon bands
summary: Bands rode furniture wagons through the city on Mardi Gras, getting food and drink at houses and saloons.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Sure. Why would you play? Bass drum?

I would be playing on one of those wagons, see? You'd be at the wagons. Oh I see. Like a bunch of you guys, like you say, you got about eight guys that are ready to get a big furniture wagon. Put your little band, get your three or six piece band in, wagon, build a wagon. The guy would be hanging all around the wagon, riding all over the town, see? Going to people's house, like your house, going to your house. You get a guy like, live across town. You live this way. The other guy will live here. Maybe we've had two, three guys living in Oakland. Well the wagon go all around, looking around, see all those guys. See the friends, huh? Yeah. And everywhere you go, they had donuts and beer and stuff for you when you come in. They know you were coming? And they have that for the mardi Gras. That's what it used to be down there. So you could stop by the ground, you could stop anywhere and go in the house and get the donuts and stuff off the table. Like an open house? Yeah. See, they talk about, that's been going on around the audience for years. And every saloon you pass, you got a good band, they call you off the way and give you a drink. On Mardi Gras Day. Any day, on Sundays, when we advertise them. See, because when a band come on the corner playing, that guy make more money. So the band, and somebody put a sign up there, they say, the band will be in, and it's time to stop here, but everybody going to hang around the saloon in the corner. Yes. When the cops are chasing them off the corner, well they've got to go in the saloon.
